name: Atomic Chat
qwen_support: Open-source local-AI app (fork of Jan) running Qwen GGUFs through its own llama.cpp fork (atomic-llama-cpp-turboquant), upstream llama.cpp, or MLX-VLM on Apple Silicon — all behind one OpenAI-compatible API at localhost:1337/v1. One-click agents (OpenCode, Cline, Hermes, OpenClaw). Publisher of the AtomicChat GGUF/MLX quants (own imatrix, held-out perplexity per quant).
notable_flags: TurboQuant KV cache turbo3/turbo4 on the in-house fork — up to ~4.3x smaller KV footprint, CUDA/Vulkan/CPU on macOS/Windows/Linux
DFlash2 block-diffusion drafting on 'Auto' (16 candidates ranked on next-token fit + previous-token connection)
MTP on MLX for Qwen 3.5/3.6; EAGLE-3 for Gemma 4 (Apple Silicon)
gotchas: Three swappable backends behind one API — a benchmark must state which backend ran, or the number is not attributable to an engine.

Contradiction unresolved: README says DFlash is Apple-Silicon-only, but the vendor benchmarked DFlash2 on a rented RTX 6000 (2026-08, ledger [63]). Verify NVIDIA DFlash2 status before treating those numbers as engine-attributable.
TurboQuant headline claims (8x attention, 6x KV, zero accuracy loss at 3-bit) are Google H100 research figures, not Qwen-on-consumer-hardware measurements.
Repo license is 'Other'; began as a fork of Jan (Menlo Research). Repo: github.com/AtomicBot-ai/Atomic-Chat (1.4k stars, TypeScript).

methods.label: Desktop app

steps.text: Download Atomic Chat for your system from https://atomic.chat/ and install it.

methods.note: The site lists macOS 13.6+ (Intel and Apple Silicon), Windows x64 and Linux x86_64.
